comment: Values approximate; verify against NASA sources.
notes: Thrust in newtons. Spec lists one thrust per engine: for booster-class engines it is treated as sea-level thrust and vacuum thrust is scaled by isp_vac/isp_sl (same mass flow). Vacuum-only engines have null sea-level values and cannot light on the pad. cost is in millions of USD (cost_tier is the spec's $ rating).

engines.name: Redstone-class (alcohol/LOX)
engines.description: Cheap and weak. A good first engine for light payloads.
engines.source: Inspired by the real A-7 / Redstone engine (alcohol/LOX), 1950s-60s.

engines.name: Kerosene booster (RP-1/LOX)
engines.source: Inspired by real RP-1/LOX engines such as the Atlas MA-5 / Thor LR-79 family, 1950s-60s.

engines.name: Hypergolic upper
engines.description: Restartable and reliable, but toxic. Vacuum only.
engines.source: Inspired by real storable-propellant upper-stage engines such as Aerojet AJ10 / Titan II LR-91, 1960s.

engines.name: Hydrogen upper (LH2/LOX)
engines.description: Best efficiency of the catalog, but its tanks are bulky.
engines.source: Inspired by the real Pratt & Whitney RL10 / Rocketdyne J-2 hydrogen engines, 1960s.

engines.name: Heavy booster
engines.description: Moon-class only. Enormous thrust, enormous bill.
engines.source: Inspired by the real Rocketdyne F-1 engine (Saturn V first stage), 1960s.

engines.name: Small lander engine
engines.description: Throttleable descent engine for landing on the Moon.
engines.source: Inspired by the real Apollo Lunar Module descent engine (TRW LMDE), 1960s.
